Manning led our men with Green and Rathbone walking very easily in the middle of the field and our 4 others following. A crowd of rain-drenched cyclists waiting at Streatham were surprised to see the leaders so soon, and the hot pace caused our critics to think they could not last.
King, McMullen, Manning. Rathbone, Reeve and Rickards, all of whom have done some good times in previous championships.
Whit-monday found our friend Manning having his annual constitutional between Norwich and Ipswich (42 miles), but this time he was beaten into second place.
McMullen, Dodkin, Cricton, Carne and Rathbone have already promised to be there, and they, with Green Rickards, and Manning, will make a redoubtable team.
During, the Easter holiday Stanley Manning made his customary trip to the Eastern Counties and finished second in the Ipswich—Norwich race, a distance of 42 miles.

Starting in rather a narrow roadway the field was well bunched up for some 440 yards, where the first glimpse of our men was seen, and a hasty check showed Green 9th, McMullen 14th, Cooper 15th, Field 26th and Manning 47th.

Rathbone came along next, walking quite comfortably and with lots of strength in hand. Manning and Wattam pleased the crowd, as also did Bidgood. Fletcher came along in the last group, smiling and determined.
The Belgrave team (Green, Rathbone, Manning) was successful in the team race by one point, from Surrey Walking Club. An interesting debûtant in our Three Miles Road Run at Wimbledon was T.
